question.text:
A factory with $150$ machines produces $600 \, 000$ baseball balls weekly. To determine the number of balls produced by a machine on average, the owner of the factory uses the formula $$ P = \dfrac{b}{m}, $$ where $b$ is the number of balls produced by the factory weekly, and $m$ is the number of machines in the factory.

What is an appropriate measurement unit for $P?$
question.explanation:
We are solving for measurement units, so we can ignore the quantities $150$ and $600\,000.$ They do not matter, if we are just solving for units.

Since $b$ represents $\text{balls}$ and $m$ represents $\text{machines},$ the appropriate measurement unit for $P = \dfrac{b}{m}$ is $\dfrac{\text{balls}}{\text{machines}}.$

question.text: The acceleration $a$ of a body is related to applied force $F$ and mass $m$ by the equation $a = \dfrac{F}{m}.$ If $F$ is measured in Newtons $\left( \dfrac{\textrm{kg} \, \textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2} \right)$ and $m$ is measured in kilograms, determine an appropriate measurement unit for acceleration.
question.explanation:
We can find the unit of acceleration by substituting the given units of force and mass into the formula and simplifying.

\begin{align*} a & = \dfrac{F}{m}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left( \dfrac{\textrm{kg} \, \textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2} \right)}{\textrm{kg}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cancel{\textrm{kg}} \, \textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2 \, \cancel{\textrm{kg}}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2} \end{align*}

Thus, the unit of acceleration is $\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2}.$

example.title: Finding Units When There Is Cancellation

question.text: The speed of a car moving with a constant acceleration is given by the formula $v=at,$ where $a$ is the car's acceleration, and $t$ is the time passed. Given that the acceleration is measured in $\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2}$, determine the units of speed in terms of meters and seconds.
question.explanation:
Acceleration is measured in $\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2}$ and time is measured in seconds. We can find the unit of speed by substituting the given units of acceleration and time into the formula and simplifying. \begin{align} \require{cancel} v & = a\cdot t\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2} \cdot \textrm{s} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{m} \, \cancel{\textrm{s}}}{\textrm{s}^{\cancel{2}}} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}} \end{align}

Thus, the unit of speed is $\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}}.$
